chung.Time Allocation: Study hour (150h) = 45h (60 sessions) contact hours + 1h final exam + 104h self-study
chung.Description:
-Main objective: This course equips students with:

(1) Understanding the Regulatory and Conceptual Frameworks

(2) Practical Preparation of Financial Statements

(3) Advanced Group Accounting and Consolidation

(4) Analysis and Interpretation of Financial Data

(5) Specialized and Simplified Reporting

-Description: Students will master the conceptual and regulatory frameworks of IFRS alongside the practical skills needed to prepare individual and consolidated financial statements.They will develop technical expertise in applying standards to complex areas including revenue recognition, taxation, and group accounting. Furthermore, learners acquire the ability to evaluate an entity's financial health and investment potential by synthesizing cash flow trends, earnings metrics, and segmental performance to support economic decision-making. Finally, students gain insight into specialized reporting environments, including hyperinflationary economies and the IFRS for SMEs standard.

-Teaching method: The course applies diverse pedagogical approaches such as lectures, analytical discussions, presentation skills, collaborative group work, case studies, problem-based learning. Assessment is integrated through applied exercises, situational analysis, and teamwork performance.
chung.StudentTasks:
- Students must attend more than 80% of contact slots in order to be accepted to the final examination.

- Student is responsible to do all exercises, assignments given by instructor in class or at home and submit on time

- Use laptop in class only for learning purpose

- Read the textbook in advance

- Access the course website (http://flm.fpt.edu.vn) for up-to-date information and material of the course, for online supports from teachers and other students and for practicing and assessment.

taiLieu: International Financial Reporting: A Practical Guide
clo: Explain the IASB regulatory and conceptual frameworks, while applying relevant standards for the presentation of financial statements, the selection of accounting policies, and the correction of accounting errors
Outline specific IFRS/IAS requirements for the recognition and measurement of key financial elements, including non-current assets, revenue, and financial instruments
Construct consolidated financial statements for groups of companies, performing accurate calculations for goodwill, intra-group eliminations, and non-controlling interests
Perform evaluating an entity's financial health and investment potential by synthesizing cash flow trends, earnings metrics, and segmental performance to support economic decision-making
Critique the impact of specialized reporting areas, such as deferred taxation, leases, and potential dilution of earnings, on an entity’s perceived financial health and valuation
Integrate professional objectivity and ethical responsibility when applying international standards to ensure financial reports provide a "true and fair view" for external stakeholders
